cards.explanation: The answer is False. Paul says, "It is no trouble for me to write the same things to you again…" (Philippians 3:1). Nobody's rolling their eyes at the pen here, friends. He says it's no trouble, and he calls it a safeguard for them.

The answer is a safeguard for them. Paul says writing the same things again is "…a safeguard for you." (Philippians 3:1). A safeguard keeps you protected, like an oven mitt for the soul. Hearing it twice is not a waste when it keeps you safe.
The answer is Christ Jesus. Paul says they are the ones "…who glory in Christ Jesus…" (Philippians 3:3). Their pride and their joy sit on Him, not on themselves, friends. Nice and clear.

The answer is False. Paul says they are the ones "…who put no confidence in the flesh…" (Philippians 3:3). Their trust sits somewhere else entirely, friends. They worship by the Spirit of God and glory in Christ Jesus.

The answer is more. Paul says, "If anyone else thinks he has grounds for confidence in the flesh, I have more…" (Philippians 3:4). He's about to lay out a résumé that would make anybody sit up straight. Hold onto your aprons, bakers.

The answer is True. Paul says, "as to righteousness in the law, faultless." (Philippians 3:6). That's the top of his list, and he puts it there on purpose, friends. It makes what he says next hit even harder.

The answer is True. Paul says, "But whatever was gain to me I count as loss for the sake of Christ." (Philippians 3:7). Everything he used to stack up as a win, he now counts as loss. That's quite a turn, bakers.

The answer is knowing Christ Jesus his Lord. Paul counts all things as loss compared to "…the surpassing excellence of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord…" (Philippians 3:8). Nothing else comes close to that, friends. Paul even says he has lost all things for Him.

The answer is as rubbish. Paul says, "I consider them rubbish, that I may gain Christ" (Philippians 3:8). Not a small word, friends, and Paul meant it. Compared to knowing Christ, it all goes in the bin.

The answers are law and faith. Paul says he does not want "…my own righteousness from the law…" (Philippians 3:9). He had a faultless record there, and he still lets it go, friends. He wants the righteousness that is "…through faith in Christ, the righteousness from God on the basis of faith." (Philippians 3:9). It comes from God, not from our own record.

The answer is False. Paul wants the power of Christ's resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings together, friends. He writes, "I want to know Christ and the power of His resurrection and the fellowship of His sufferings, being conformed to Him in His death…" (Philippians 3:10).

The answer is the resurrection from the dead. Paul says, "…and so, somehow, to attain to the resurrection from the dead." (Philippians 3:11). That's where the whole passage lands, bakers. It's the goal he's reaching for.
